why: The Cloud Core asks for 'the PDFs in my Documents'. It cannot name that folder: only the
device knows where the owner's Documents actually is, and the owner may have moved it.
So the Cloud Core sends a BUCKET NAME and the device resolves it - then confines it by
the owner's authorised roots exactly as it confines an absolute path. A bucket name is
therefore never more authority than a path; it is less, because it cannot name anywhere
Until 2026-09-12 this was not a contract, it was an assumption. The Cloud Core put the
bucket name straight into payload.roots and the device answered 'payload.roots must be
absolute paths'. The refusal was recorded on 2026-09-09 (ADR-0102, the defect sink) and
the search stayed broken: both halves had tests, neither read the other.

roots_field.absent_or_empty: the device searches every authorised root
entry_forms: an absolute path (resolved, then confined by the authorised roots)
a bucket name followed by relative segments, e.g. `documents/Faturalar` - resolved under the bucket, then confined
refused: a relative path that does not begin with a bucket name
a bucket whose folder this machine does not have, or which resolves outside the authorised roots

read_by: services/api/app/documents/service.py (the Cloud Core sends only these names)
